llm.summary: The skill's description claims powerful auto-update behavior (reads cron, waits for idle, updates core & skills, restarts gateway, notifies external services) but the package is instruction-only and fails to declare required binaries, config paths, credentials, or the referenced scripts—this mismatch is concerning and needs developer/source proof before trust.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a Windows PowerShell-based updater that uses npm + clawhub CLI, reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json, and sends Telegram/Feishu notifications. The registry metadata lists no required binaries, no required config paths, and no credentials. Requiring no env vars/binaries/configs is inconsistent with the claimed purpose (auto-updating core/skills, restarting gateway, and sending notifications).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions reference running scripts (scripts/self-updater.ps1) and reading user config files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json) and performing network/notification actions. There are no shipped scripts or code files in the package, and the registry did not declare those config paths—this is scope creep and a practical gap. The skill also claims to auto-detect/send notifications to external services without declaring where tokens come from.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only), which minimizes automatic installation risk but is contradictory here because SKILL.md expects local scripts to exist (scripts/self-updater.ps1). Absence of those files means the skill is incomplete or relies on out-of-band delivery; either case is a red flag requiring the author/source to provide the actual implementation and install steps.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill will likely need PowerShell, npm, clawhub CLI, network access, and credentials for Telegram/Feishu, plus permission to update core and restart the gateway—none are declared. It also states it reads user config files but registry shows no required config paths. Updating core and restarting services typically requires elevated privileges; these are not surfaced or justified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and is user-invocable; autonomous invocation is allowed (the platform default) but there is no evidence the skill requests persistent system-wide privileges or modifies other skills' configs. That said, the update/restart behavior implies privilege needs that are not declared.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or enable this skill yet. It currently contains only a README (SKILL.md) but references local PowerShell scripts and config files that are not present and does not declare required binaries or credentials. Before trusting it, ask the publisher for: (1) the actual scripts/source code to review (scripts/self-updater.ps1 and any helper code), (2) exact install instructions and any network endpoints used for fetching updates (and whether updates are signed), (3) required binaries and permission/privilege needs, (4) how Telegram/Feishu tokens are provided and stored, and (5) evidence that it will not modify other skills or exfiltrate config. If you must run updates, do so manually in a safe/test environment, ensure backups and rollback, and prefer least-privilege execution (no automatic restarts on production until audited).
